Section 4 of the IPCC AR6 Synthesis Report contrasts the decarbonization of light industry and manufacturing with the reduction of cement process emissions as follows:

*   **Light industry and manufacturing:** These sectors can be "largely decarbonized" through the use of available abatement technologies, such as material efficiency and circularity, electrification (e.g., heat pumps, electrothermal heating), and switching to low- or zero-GHG emitting fuels like hydrogen, ammonia, and bio-based or synthetic fuels [chunk_id: ipcc-ar6-syr-2023:p121:text:c001].
*   **Cement process emissions:** Deep reductions in this sector are more challenging and will rely on the substitution of cementitious materials and the availability of Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) until new chemistries are mastered [chunk_id: ipcc-ar6-syr-2023:p121:text:c001]. 

While light industry relies on readily available technologies for broad decarbonization, cement production requires specific material substitution and CCS infrastructure to address its process-related emissions [chunk_id: ipcc-ar6-syr-2023:p121:text:c001]. [ipcc-ar6-syr-2023:p121:text:c001]

Health and Nutrition
C.3.7 Human health will benefit from integrated mitigation and adaptation options that mainstream health into food,
infrastructure, social protection, and water policies (very high confidence). Effective adaptation options exist to help
protect human health and well-being, including: strengthening public health programs related to climate-sensitive
diseases, increasing health systems resilience, improving ecosystem health, improving access to potable water,
reducing exposure of water and sanitation systems to flooding, improving surveillance and early warning systems,
vaccine development (very high confidence), improving access to mental healthcare, and Heat Health Action Plans that
include early warning and response systems (high confidence). Adaptation strategies which reduce food loss and waste
or support balanced, sustainable healthy diets contribute to nutrition, health, biodiversity and other environmental
benefits (high confidence). {4.5.5} (Figure SPM.7)
